rows.claim: a tools/call carrying no _meta at all is rejected with -32022, not -32602
rows.evidence: dispatch_test.exs:101-105 — `Dispatch.dispatch(req("tools/call", %{"name" => "whoami"}), ctx("PM"), config())` sends params with no `_meta`, and `assert resp["error"]["code"] == -32_022`. The OC check's `missing-meta` fixture is exactly that request shape — `{slug:`missing-meta`,...,params:{},rpcId:101}` — and its single axis requires -32602. A one-axis check with a contradicting claim is `:contradicting` whole, so this is 4a with nothing silent to soften it.

rows.claim: in JSON mode subscriptions/listen is refused with -32601 inside an HTTP 200 response
rows.evidence: subscriptions_stream_test.exs:1028-1029 — `assert response.status == 200` and `assert response.body["error"]["code"] == -32_601`, over a real socket through `Req`. The OC axis `te.status!==404` is `fail_when_true` and requires 404; this unit asserts 200 and PASSES, so the claim contradicts it. The code axis agrees. Contradiction beats silence in `shape_from_axes/1`, so the edge is `:contradicting` and lands 4a.

rows.note: THE SLICE'S SHARPEST FINDING, and the only edge in it that contradicts an axis it ALSO agrees with on the same check. Our SDK and the harness agree on WHICH JSON-RPC error an unimplemented method earns and disagree on the HTTP status it rides on — and this unit does not merely fail to assert 404, it asserts 200 and is green. Every other red-OC edge in this slice is silent on `http_status` because the unit never looks at it; this one looked, and wrote down the other answer.
oc_key: If the server does not implement the requested RPC method, it MUST respond with 404 Not Found and a JSON-RPC error with code -32601 (Method not found).
